images.title: Count the places
images.purpose: Recap the rule of decimal places: the digits after the point in the two numbers add up to the digits after the point in the product.
images.composition: One short vertical multiplication sits in the centre, numbers right aligned, with a place count tag to the right of each row; white space around.
exact_structure: A vertical layout of 3 rows, all numbers right aligned in large dark text #1F2937, centred in the frame.
Row 1: "2.3"; to its right a teal #0072B2 tag "1 place".
Row 2: "× 0.14"; to its right an amber #E69F00 tag "2 places".
A single grey #6B7280 horizontal rule line under row 2.
Row 3 under the rule: "0.322" in reddish purple #CC79A7; to its right a reddish purple #CC79A7 tag "1 + 2 = 3 places".
No partial products, no carried digits, no other numbers or text.
rejection: place counts other than 1, 2 and 3 on the three rows
partial products or extra working rows drawn
images.takeaway: The product has as many decimal places as the two numbers together: 1 + 2 = 3.
images.description: A vertical multiplication of 2.3 by 0.14 giving 0.322, with tags 1 place, 2 places and 1 + 2 = 3 places beside the rows.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept as a compact recap of the rule before the questions.
images.teaching_notes: Read the place tags down the side and check that the first two add to the third.

image_decisions.why: A compact column recap of the rule supports the practice questions without giving any answer away.
